desc: National Fertilizers Limited (NFL) Nangal plant is a major fertilizer production facility located in Nangal, Punjab. Established in 1960, it was one of the first public sector fertilizer plants in India. The plant produces urea and other nitrogenous fertilizers using natural gas as feedstock. It played a critical role in India's Green Revolution by supplying fertilizers to Punjab and Haryana. The plant is located near the Bhakra Nangal Dam, which provides hydroelectric power for its operations.
fact: It was one of the first public sector fertilizer plants in India, established in 1960 · It produced urea crucial for India's Green Revolution · It uses natural gas as feedstock · It is located near Bhakra Nangal Dam for power supply

desc: Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers (RCF) Trombay plant is located in the Chembur suburb of Mumbai, Maharashtra. Established in 1965, it produces urea, complex fertilizers, and industrial chemicals. The plant uses naphtha and natural gas as feedstocks and operates multiple production units. RCF is one of India's largest fertilizer companies and the Trombay plant serves the agricultural markets of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and southern states. The plant also produces ammonia, methanol, and ammonium bicarbonate for industrial use.
fact: It was established in 1965 in Chembur, Mumbai · It produces urea, complex fertilizers, and industrial chemicals · It uses naphtha and natural gas as feedstocks · It serves agricultural markets of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and southern India

desc: Coromandel International's fertilizer plant in Visakhapatnam is one of the largest phosphatic fertilizer plants in India. Established in 1961, the plant produces DAP (diammonium phosphate), NPK complex fertilizers, and single superphosphate. The plant is strategically located near Visakhapatnam Port for importing raw materials including rock phosphate and phosphoric acid. It serves the agricultural markets of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, and parts of central India. The plant is part of the Murugappa Group and uses advanced manufacturing technology.
fact: It is one of India's largest phosphatic fertilizer plants, established in 1961 · It produces DAP, NPK, and single superphosphate · It is located near Visakhapatnam Port for raw material imports · It is part of the Murugappa Group serving southern and eastern India

desc: IFFCO's Phulpur plant is a major fertilizer production facility located in the Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh. Established in 1988, it is one of the largest urea-producing plants in India. The plant is operated by the Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative (IFFCO), the world's largest cooperative fertilizer company. It produces urea and other nitrogenous fertilizers using natural gas as feedstock. The plant serves the agricultural needs of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh and is known for its energy-efficient production processes.
fact: It is one of the largest urea-producing plants in India, established in 1988 · It is operated by IFFCO, the world's largest cooperative fertilizer company · It produces urea using natural gas feedstock · It serves Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh

desc: Kribhco's Hazira plant is a major fertilizer facility located near Surat, Gujarat. Established in 1986, it is operated by the Krishak Bharati Cooperative (Kribhco). The plant produces urea using natural gas supplied from the Hazira offshore gas fields. It has a production capacity of over 1.5 million metric tons per year, making it one of the largest urea plants in India. The plant serves the agricultural markets of Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Kribhco is known for its cooperative ownership model and rural development initiatives.
fact: Kribhco Hazira is one of the largest urea plants in India at 1.5 million MT/year · It uses natural gas from the Hazira offshore gas fields · Established in 1986, operated by Kribhco cooperative · It serves Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra

desc: IFFCO's Kandla plant is a major phosphatic fertilizer complex located near Deendayal Port in Kutch, Gujarat. Established in 1989, the plant produces DAP and NPK complex fertilizers. Its strategic location adjacent to Kandla Port enables efficient handling of imported raw materials including rock phosphate, ammonia, and phosphoric acid. The plant serves the agricultural markets of Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh. It features state-of-the-art pollution control systems and is ISO certified for quality management.
fact: It produces DAP and NPK complex fertilizers near Deendayal Port · Its strategic port location enables efficient raw material imports · Established in 1989, it serves northern and western Indian agriculture · It features advanced pollution control and ISO certification
